podcast.title: Band Disbanded in 1997
podcast.body: The dance act D:Ream, which featured Brian Cox on keyboards, ended in 1997. "When the band died in 1997, he continued with his education earning a doctorate in philosophy and working with high energy particle physics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brian Cox's Parallel Careers
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, Brian Cox was a keyboardist in the electro-pop band Dream while simultaneously pursuing his PhD in physics. He is now Professor Brian Cox, a prominent British scientist involved with the Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland. "Back in the early 90s, Brian played keyboards in an electro pop band called Dream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

awards.title: Grammy Award for Best New Age Album (1992)

xref.title: Physicist and Academic
xref.body: While playing keyboards for the dance act D:Ream (referred to as "Dream" in the transcript), Brian Cox studied physics at the University of Manchester. After the band ended in 1997, he continued his education, earning a doctorate in philosophy and working in high-energy particle physics, including at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland. "When he was playing keyboards with them, he studied physics at the University of Manchester."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
